topStories.headline: HANC Takes Aim at Lurie's Homeless-Services Overhaul, Calling It a Threat to Affordable Housing
topStories.dek: The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council convened its November meeting to hear advocates argue that Mayor Lurie's plan to re-bid all homelessness contracts could gut permanent supportive housing in the neighborhood.
topStories.body:
The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council held its monthly meeting on November 12 at the Park Branch Library community room, centering the evening on Mayor Daniel Lurie's August announcement that the city will competitively re-award its entire portfolio of homelessness service and housing contracts through May 2029. HANC board member Christin Evans, in a post published November 7, described the reprocurement plan as a potential vehicle to defund permanent supportive housing — a characterization sharply disputed by the Lurie administration.

Jennifer Friedenbach, executive director of the Coalition on Homelessness, and Joe Wilson, executive director of Hospitality House, both attended to lay out concerns. The administration launched the overhaul on August 31, saying contracts would be reoriented around measurable outcomes rather than reimbursing nonprofits for expenses regardless of results. City officials said the restructuring could consolidate overlapping programs and shift more funding to high-performing providers.

Critics, including HANC, contend that placing all permanent supportive housing contracts back out to competitive bid creates risks for existing tenants and the nonprofits that serve them. Supporters of the plan — including District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood — argue that years of city audits have documented the need for stronger accountability in a system that spends more than $500 million annually.

The November 12 meeting also included an election for the HANC board, with the new term running from December 2026 through November 2027. Calvin Welch presented an analysis of how Haight-Ashbury precincts voted in the November 3 general election.

topStories.headline: Second Summit Opens on Lower Haight, Giving Used Outdoor Gear a New Life
topStories.dek: A new consignment shop at 583 Haight Street fills a gap in the city's outdoor-gear market, stocking skis, climbing equipment, bikes, and camping supplies just as ski season gets underway.
topStories.body:
Second Summit, San Francisco's first dedicated outdoor-gear consignment shop, opened recently at 583 Haight Street in the Lower Haight, drawing notice from the SF Standard on November 9. The store operates on a straightforward consignment model: customers bring in used skis, climbing shoes, tents, sleeping pads, bikes, and other gear; the owner prices and sells each item, keeping a share of the proceeds.

The shop stocks a broad range of used equipment covering hiking, camping, backpacking, skiing, snowboarding, cycling, and trail running, all at a fraction of retail prices. The store's stated goal is to keep quality gear in circulation and make outdoor adventure more financially accessible to city residents.

Second Summit is open Thursday through Sunday, noon to 6 p.m. The owner has also said he plans to host community events including introductory courses on backpacking and climbing, and possibly a weekly run club. The shop's website is 2nd-summit.com.

topStories.headline: Panhandle Loses Its Community Bulletin Board — And Nobody Knows Why
topStories.dek: A well-used neighborhood notice board near the public restrooms in the Panhandle vanished about a month ago without any public announcement, leaving residents searching for answers.
topStories.body:
A community bulletin board that stood near the public restrooms in the Panhandle — in the stretch of park between Oak and Fell streets and Ashbury and Clayton streets — disappeared roughly a month ago, the Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council reported on November 7. The two-sided board was a popular resource for local notices, flyers, and community information, used by both residents and park visitors.

According to HANC board member Lisa Awbrey, who wrote about the disappearance, no public notice was given before the board was removed. It is not yet clear whether the removal was ordered by SF Recreation and Parks, was accidental, or was the result of some other action. HANC said local residents and regular Panhandle users rely on the board and have been left without explanation.

The Panhandle is one of the most heavily used green corridors in these neighborhoods, connecting Haight-Ashbury to Golden Gate Park. Anyone with information about what happened to the bulletin board is encouraged to contact HANC through hanc-sf.org.

moreNews.headline: Greystar Breaks Ground at 400 Divisadero on 203-Unit Building
moreNews.body: Construction began on October 19 at the long-vacant former Touchless Car Wash site at 400 Divisadero Street, where national apartment developer Greystar is building an eight-story, 203-unit residential building with ground-floor retail. The project, which broke a logjam that had stalled housing at the site for nearly a decade, will be the largest housing development along the Divisadero corridor. Only 20 of the 203 units are designated as permanently affordable. HANC and housing advocates have raised concerns about Greystar's track record as a landlord; Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and pro-housing groups have backed the project as a needed addition to the neighborhood's housing stock.

restaurants.name: Magnolia Brewing – Haight
restaurants.description: Haight Street's landmark craft brewery and gastropub, reopened in late 2024 under new local ownership with a refreshed taproom, house-brewed beers, and elevated pub food.

restaurants.name: The Alembic

restaurants.name: Pork Store Cafe
restaurants.description: Much-loved Haight Street diner serving enormous portions of scratch-made breakfast and brunch at affordable prices since 1989.

restaurants.name: Escape From New York Pizza

restaurants.name: Zazie

restaurants.name: Beit Rima
restaurants.description: Award-winning Cole Valley spot serving Arabic comfort food — hand-kneaded bread, crispy falafel, chicken skewers, and za'atar-dusted pita — with a devoted neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Cole Valley Tavern
restaurants.description: Neighborhood go-to American bar with a warm dining room, rotating food specials, and an ice cream window that draws lines on warm evenings.

restaurants.name: InoVino

restaurants.name: Crepes On Cole
restaurants.description: Casual Cole Valley standby open late most nights, offering sweet and savory crêpes, burgers, and beer in a relaxed neighbourhood setting.

restaurants.name: Toronado
restaurants.description: Lower Haight craft-beer pilgrimage site with 50 taps of rare and sought-after brews, sticker-plastered walls, and a cash-only, no-nonsense vibe — now under new local ownership as of June 2026.

restaurants.name: Bar Jabroni
restaurants.description: Lively Lower Haight wine bar pouring chilled reds and orange wines alongside small plates like beef tartare with Szechuan peppercorns and house-made focaccia.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Organic, from-scratch Mexican cooking from the Nopa team, plating blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and mole made with local and sustainable ingredients.

restaurants.name: Noc Noc
restaurants.description: Lower Haight bar with trippy, Tim Burton-esque décor that is a neighbourhood fixture — only in San Francisco.

restaurants.name: Danny Coyle's
restaurants.description: Friendly Lower Haight Irish bar open until 2am, with a great tap selection, sports on TV, and a loyal neighbourhood crowd.

restaurants.name: Woods Lowside
restaurants.description: Casual Lower Haight bar with crisp, dry house beers, natural wines, Detroit-style pizza from Joyride Pizza on site, and a heated back patio.

restaurants.name: Bambino's Ristorante
restaurants.description: Charming old-school Italian restaurant in Cole Valley with hearty classic pastas and a warm, neighbourhood trattoria feel.

restaurants.name: Double Black
restaurants.description: New Cole Valley coffee shop inside the Yardsale outdoor apparel store, drawing queues for iced hojicha lattes with black-sesame cold foam.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, this 1904 Beaux Arts Victorian hotel sits across from Golden Gate Park and includes a daily continental breakfast and weekday wine-and-cheese reception.

hotels.name: The Metro Hotel
hotels.description: Family-owned 23-room boutique hotel on Divisadero with original artwork throughout, a private garden, and a welcoming eco-conscious ethos steps from Haight-Ashbury.

shops.name: Booksmith
shops.description: Haight Street's landmark independent bookstore since 1976, offering a wide selection of new titles and hosting more than 200 author events per year.

shops.name: Amoeba Music
shops.description: Enormous independent music store claiming the world's largest selection of new and used vinyl, CDs, DVDs, and posters — a pilgrimage site for music fans since 1990.

shops.name: Love on Haight
shops.description: SF Legacy Business since 1989 selling vibrant tie-dye clothing and accessories by more than 175 local and international artists, keeping the Haight's countercultural spirit alive.

shops.name: Wasteland
shops.description: Glamorous Haight Street vintage and resale boutique with a carefully curated mix of high-end secondhand fashion and designer pieces — buy, sell, or trade.

shops.name: Piedmont Boutique
shops.description: An unofficial Haight landmark identifiable by the giant fishnet-stocking legs hanging from the second-floor window, selling costumes, festival wear, and dramatic accessories.

shops.name: Relic Vintage
shops.description: Go-to Haight Street vintage shop since 2012, housing carefully selected garments from the 1920s through the 1980s and a strong collection of statement accessories.

shops.name: Say Cheese
shops.description: Cole Valley institution since 1976 offering an extensive world cheese selection alongside charcuterie, wines, olives, artisanal snacks, and loaded deli sandwiches.

shops.name: San Francisco Mercantile
shops.description: Haight Street retail shop partnered with San Francisco Heritage, selling locally made gifts, detailed neighborhood maps, art, and keepsakes by Bay Area artists.

shops.name: Woot Bear

shops.name: Cole Hardware

artEntertainment.type: Non-profit poster art gallery and printmaking studio
